steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Here, the data you asked for.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Thanks, Ferdinand. I didn't think you'd hand it over personally.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: We were able to retrieve most of the Loken Watertank data thanks to you. The fewer that know about this, the better.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And I'm curious as to why you wanted these data.
She gazes at the monitor in front of her, so focused that even her breathing slows down.
A video of a girl with white hair is playing.
The girl spends most of her time sleeping, eating, or sitting in a corner with a blank look on her face.
From time to time, she is led into a lab, where she crushes furniture placed in a room separated by a 1-meter thick wall.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: What a beautiful child.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You remind me of Loken Williams. I thought only madmen boast about their test subjects.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Sure, he's been accused of crossing a moral line.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Morals are shackles that the short-sighted impose upon themselves.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Science has never been bound by common sense. There is no greater insult to a scientist than to be judged by moral standards.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Williams's problem was that he allowed the infinite unknown to get the better of his sanity, and he abandoned the logic and reason a scientist must grip.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: See at the end of the video how your 'beautiful child' turned the lab into a nightmarish catastrophe.
The monitor is showing a different image.
There is no recorded sound, but the screams seem to pierce the screen and fill a lab from another time.
The fallen debris does not hide the bloodstains.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: What happened to the girl?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Records pertaining to her have been tampered with. Like the other legacies of Loken Watertank, she has value to somebody, somewhere.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I want to find her.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: May I assume you're considering ending Williams's experiments?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: She is too difficult to control. A risk Rhine Lab cannot afford.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: She didn't volunteer to be a test subject. I can't ask something so cruel of her.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You want to heal her?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: We're not doctors, but anyone whose seen the experiments in their entirety should not harbor such delusions.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: No, Ferdinand.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: All I want to do is find her... and give her a hug.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: A... a hug?

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: The girl... she's all alone.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: They took her family from her, and made her something entirely different from all other people.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I can't help but think... where is she now?

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Has she made new friends? Or new enemies?

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I want to hear her voice...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I can't change her past, but the future may not be lost yet.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You know, Dorothy... I really have no idea what you're thinking at times.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Not many scientists are as sentimental as you are. You're not bound by logic or reason either. Perhaps, one day, your madness will put Williams's to shame...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Madness? I've seen this in my dreams, many times.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: That's why I want to find the girl.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: If she's still alive... if anyone can save her from her past...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Then maybe someone will be there to stop me, if I really do go over the edge.
